Change detection

Every change. Explained.

Driftly snapshots every page on a schedule and tells you, in plain language, what changed since last time — and why it matters. Drag to compare a real check of the demo store.

  • Headline rewritten
  • Sale banner added
  • “Browse products” → “Start shopping”
  • Navigation renamed

Security

Security without the noise.

A passive review of what a visitor’s browser received — headers, cookies, forms and scripts — graded, explained as attack paths, with the fix. Nothing is attacked.

Driftly

Performance

Speed you can see.

Lab tests on phone, tablet or desktop profiles: Core Web Vitals, waterfall, filmstrip, budgets — and the fixes that matter most.

Driftly

API testing

Your site’s APIs, in every check.

Start from the calls your site already makes. Chain them into flows — log in, pass the token, add to cart — assert every step, and export to Postman, OpenAPI or test code.

Testing an API in depth? Meet Prism

Driftly

Recorder

Your key flows, in every check.

Record the flows that matter — sign in, add to cart, check out — and Driftly replays them on every check, repairs locators that drift and tells you what it healed. Export them as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, WebdriverIO or Puppeteer code when you need to.

Building a whole test suite? Meet Tracemend

Driftly

Bug reports

Bugs, written for you.

Press Report bug on any change, finding, failed request or test. Driftly writes the steps, expected and actual, attaches screenshots, console errors and failed requests — and files it to Jira, GitHub, Linear or Azure DevOps.

Driftly

Release checks

One answer: GO or NO‑GO.

Before you ship, one run across visual, security, performance, API and recorded tests — with every blocking rule, its evidence, and a comparison with the last release.

GO

NO-GO

  • GO
  • GO WITH WARNINGS
  • NO-GO
Driftly

Monitoring

Always watching.

Schedule API runs, replays, performance tests, security reviews and release checks — hourly, after every check or at set times — and hear about it the moment one starts failing.

Driftly

CI

Gate every merge.

driftly ci runs the same release check on your runner and fails the build on a NO-GO — with JUnit, SARIF, Markdown and JSON for your pipeline.

Read-only dashboards

Share without sharing.

Hand stakeholders one self-contained HTML file — no server, no network requests, secrets redacted, optional password.

Which one do you need?

Three tools, three jobs. All free, all on your own computer.

  • DriftlyYou’re here

    Know if a release is safe to ship.

    Watches your live sites — visual changes, security, speed and APIs — and gives one GO or NO-GO before each release. Its recorder replays a few key flows inside those checks.

  • Tracemend

    Build the test suite you keep.

    Turns flows you record into Playwright, Selenium, Cypress or WebdriverIO code your team owns — with page objects, accessibility checks, phones and tablets, and a CLI for CI — and keeps it healing as the site changes.

    Meet Tracemend

  • Prism

    Test your API, flow by flow.

    A workspace for API testing: requests chained into flows, checks on every response, load tests, a mock server and code in 15 formats — with a command-line runner for CI.

    Meet Prism

How to verify your download

Compute the SHA-256 of the file

Get-FileHash "$HOME\Downloads\Driftly Setup 0.1.0.exe" -Algorithm SHA256

Compute the SHA-256 of the file

shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/"Driftly Setup 0.1.0.exe"

Compute the SHA-256 of the file

shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/"Driftly Setup 0.1.0.exe"
# or: sha256sum ~/Downloads/"Driftly Setup 0.1.0.exe"

Compare the result with the SHA-256 published next to the file. If they differ, delete the file and download it again.

What’s new in 0.1.0

v0.1.010 Oct 2026
  • First public release, for Windows 10 and 11 (x64).
  • Website change monitoring with plain-language summaries, noise control, approved baselines and a time machine for every page.
  • Security, Performance, API and Recorder testing windows.
  • Release checks with a GO / NO-GO verdict, scheduled monitoring and driftly ci for pipelines.
  • Bug reports from any change, finding or failed test: steps, expected and actual written for you, marked-up screenshots, capture mode, duplicate warnings and filing to Jira, GitHub, Linear or Azure DevOps.
  • Read-only dashboards exported as a single offline HTML file.
  • Automatic updates are off until you turn them on in Settings.
